rfm_tuples.R: Implied by management's strategic narrative and a $1.15B 2032 convertible-funded share repurchase (announced/executed Nov 2025): management views the equity as undervalued and is committed to it.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B (implied verification) — parse Form 4 ownership.xml for ALL transactions by named insiders in the 12 months pre-cutoff (2025-05-25 to 2026-05-25). Specifically look for open-market PURCHASES (code P) by C-suite and directors into the -31% drawdown.
rfm_tuples.M_source: form4 (m_sources.form4 — EDGAR ownership.xml direct parse over 58 Form 4 filings)
rfm_tuples.M_value: ZERO code-P (open-market purchase) transactions by any insider in the 12-month window. 162 non-derivative + derivative transactions parsed: 92 M (option exercises), 30 F (tax-withholding), 37 A (grants/awards, including the 1,728,688-RSU 'separation grant' to outgoing CEO Bradford), 3 S (open-market sales, $2.07M total). Sellers: CTO/COO Monnig $581K (2025-09-09), 10%+ holder Cavaleri $496K (2025-12-05), director Wood $997K (2025-12-23). Latest Form 4 cluster on 2026-05-14 (the most recent insider transaction filings before cutoff) — CEO Schultz, CFO Vecchiarelli, EVP Garrison, CTO Monnig — all routine M/F exercise+withhold, no opportunistic open-market purchase. Despite a -31% drawdown, an immediate new CEO transition (Aug 2025), an $807M YTD net loss, and a $1.15B convertible-funded buyback signal of management 'commitment,' not a single insider bought a share on the open market.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongest Mode-B catch in the file. The narrative says 'we are using convertible proceeds to buy back our shares because we believe they are undervalued.' The forensic tape says: none of the people making that decision wanted to take any personal risk to participate in that 'undervalued' purchase. The asymmetry is total — company spent $463M of investor capital buying back shares while insiders collectively bought $0 on the open market and sold $2.07M. This is the textbook honesty-alpha SHORT tell: management is using ENTERPRISE capital to support the stock rather than PERSONAL capital.

rfm_tuples.R: Per 8-K 2025-08-11 (Item 5.02): CEO Zachary Bradford 'resigned' as President/CEO/director effective 2025-08-10 in a 'transition,' with Chairman S. Matthew Schultz appointed CEO. Separation agreement pays $950K cash + RSU grant of 1,728,688 shares (50% vested immediately, 50% vesting 8/2026 and 8/2027 'subject to ongoing compliance' with separation/release).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the Form 4 captures the separation grant structure, and Mode B — check whether the disclosure characterizes this as a routine 'transition' vs an effective departure-for-cause.
rfm_tuples.M_value: The Form 4 footnote explicitly references a 'Separation and General Release Agreement' dated 2025-08-10. The 1.73M RSU 'A-code' grant is severance with continuing-compliance vesting (highly atypical for a normal 'transition'). The replacement is the existing Executive Chairman (not an external CEO recruit), and the appointment is effective same day with no transition period. Compensation transferred to Schultz includes a separate employment agreement also dated 2025-09-04 (filed as Exhibit 10.68). The 8-K uses 'resigned' / 'transition' framing but lacks the standard 'will pursue other opportunities' / 'effective immediately' contrast — pattern consistent with a board-initiated departure dressed as a resignation.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is technically compliant but soft-pedaled. A 'continuing compliance with the separation and general release agreement' vesting trigger on 864K RSUs (~$10M at cutoff prices) is itself evidence that the company wanted enforceable non-disparagement/non-compete leverage, which the 'amicable transition' framing does not convey. Combined with the immediate, unsearched-for Chairman appointment, this reads more like a board pushed Bradford out than a voluntary resignation. Mode B: the disclosure does not say why he left.

rfm_tuples.R: From 10-Q (Q2 FY26 ended 3/31/26) Note 9 and Note 11: $1.15B 2032 convertible senior notes (0.00% coupon, Feb-2032 maturity) issued Nov 2025; $460M of proceeds 'used to repurchase common stock.' Combined with $145M from 2030 convertible proceeds previously, $605M of convertible-funded buybacks. Treasury stock balance grew from $145M (11.76M sh) to $608.19M (42.37M sh).
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check whether the structure is a value-creating buyback (cheap debt, undervalued equity) or a capital-structure arbitrage that increases dilution risk if the stock recovers (convertible holders own the upside above conversion price).
rfm_tuples.M_value: 2032 Notes initial conversion price $19.16 (52.1832 sh/$1,000); 2030 Notes initial conversion price $14.80 (67.5858 sh/$1,000). Combined if-converted dilution = 103,941,450 shares (per 10-Q EPS Note 4, currently anti-dilutive due to loss). Cutoff stock implied $11.79 (from $13.98 May-14 Form 4 reference price × ~0.84 drawdown to cutoff peg) — already below both conversion strikes. Effective economic cost of buyback: company purchased ~30.6M treasury shares at avg ~$15 (=$463M/30.6M) while writing call options worth roughly the implied-vol value of a 6-yr at-the-money zero-coupon convertible (large). Free interest is real, but option-value sold is meaningfully larger than 'cheap debt' framing implies. Additionally, $463M of cash deployed for non-operating purposes while net loss is $787M YTD and accumulated deficit ballooned $125.9M → $912.9M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch. The company frames this as 'buy back cheap stock with cheap debt' but the math is closer to 'sell call options on our own recovery, get rewarded only if stock stays below $14.80/$19.16 forever.' For a bitcoin miner where the natural fat tail is to the upside, this is the wrong-sided convertible trade. Recall the Microstrategy comparison investors will make — MSTR sells convertibles to BUY MORE bitcoin; CLSK sold convertibles to buy back stock while accumulating fewer incremental bitcoin (11,920 BTC at 3/31/26 vs 10,428 at 9/30/25, +1,492 BTC = ~$130M at $87K, well below the $463M deployed). Capital allocation is materially questionable.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-Q Q3 FY26 cash flow: 'Loss on fair value of bitcoin, net' = $470,939K for 6 months ended 3/31/26 ($224,107K for Q3 alone). Net loss 6M $787M (basic and diluted EPS $(2.94)).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the magnitude and disclosure quality of the BTC mark-to-market hit and check management's narrative around the loss.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Confirmed: $471M YTD BTC FV loss on 11,920 BTC at $97,309/BTC cost basis = $1,160M cost-basis vs FV that has clearly fallen below cost. BTC current asset on balance sheet $674.4M at 3/31/26 (down from $966.8M at 9/30/25), even though BTC holdings INCREASED by ~14% in BTC terms. Disclosure is precise, audited, segment-level. Management discusses the loss honestly in MD&A and does not attempt to non-GAAP it away.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest disclosure. The framework should NOT penalize this — bitcoin miners holding bitcoin take BTC price risk by design, and the loss is properly recognized through P&L under ASU 2023-08. This is the kind of distress the issuer is transparent about. Useful context for the SHORT thesis only insofar as it reduces equity cushion and indicates ongoing capital pressure.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 9A: 'Based on this evaluation, management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of September 30, 2025.' FY24 had FOUR distinct material weaknesses (ITGCs/general ledger, PP&E/miner deposits accounting, payroll segregation of duties, cashier's check controls). FY25 reports them as 'successfully remediated.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the remediation language exists; Mode B — assess whether the auditor change (MaloneBailey → BDO USA) is correlated with the prior-year MW disclosure, which would be a corroborating governance signal.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Confirmed: 10-K names BDO USA, P.C. (PCAOB 243) as current auditor and MaloneBailey, LLP (PCAOB 206) as prior auditor. Four FY24 MWs remediated; BDO issued clean opinion on FY25 controls. No going-concern flag in either 10-K or 10-Q (going_concern_local: NO_GOING_CONCERN, n_matches=0). Auditor change is from a small-cap specialist (MaloneBailey) to a Big-Four-adjacent national firm (BDO) — directionally an UPGRADE for governance.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Genuine PASS. Management remediated 4 distinct MWs (which included items like 'inability to safeguard cash against unauthorized cashier's check issuance' — embarrassing) and upgraded to BDO. This is real governance progress and the framework should credit it. Note: this is the cleanest positive in CLSK's file.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K: Series A Preferred Stock — 1,750,000 outstanding, held by the 'Schultz Irrevocable Trust' (S. Matthew Schultz is Grantor). Mar 24 2026 8-K (Item 3.03) discloses Board amended the Certificate of Designation to extinguish the quarterly dividend (previously '2% of EBITA payable in cash or common stock') in exchange for a one-time $30,000 dividend payment.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — quantify the related-party value transfer and assess voting concentration through the super-voting Series A.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Series A description + Mar 24, 2026 8-K Item 3.03)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Series A has (a) 45 votes per share (1.75M sh × 45 = 78.75M votes, =~31% of outstanding common-share votes 256.6M, BEFORE any common holdings by Schultz directly), and (b) conversion right of 3 common per Series A on a change-of-control (=5.25M common). The Mar 2026 amendment extinguished a 2%-of-EBITA dividend for $30K. EBITA in profitable quarters could easily be $20M+, suggesting Schultz Trust GAVE UP an asset (the dividend stream) for $30K cash. This is OPPOSITE of self-dealing — but only at face value. In context: CLSK was running deep losses in early 2026 (no EBITA, dividend stream worthless near-term), so trading a near-worthless dividend stream for $30K cash + presumably some other consideration (board harmony, retention as CEO, etc.) is rational for both sides. There is no disclosed consideration flowing back to Schultz, however, and the amendment was approved by a Board on which Schultz sits as Chairman + CEO. Conflict-of-interest disclosure is not visible in the 8-K Item 3.03 text.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch. Two flags: (1) the super-voting Series A (45 votes/share) gives a single trust controlled by the now-CEO/Chairman substantial governance leverage that the FY25 10-K describes but does not quantify as a % of voting power; (2) the Mar 2026 CoD amendment is a related-party transaction (Board amended an instrument held by the CEO's family trust) without visible independent-director-only approval disclosure in the 8-K. Both are governance hygiene gaps consistent with a founder-controlled distressed name.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied: insider transactions are unrelated to material non-public information.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-reference Form 4 transaction dates against 8-K/earnings calendar; calculate proximate sales near events.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 58 Form 4 filings; 33 total 'sale' events (counting all dispositions including F-code withholds); ~$7.2M total disposition value (mostly F-code zero-priced tax-withholding, not market sales); 2 proximate transactions near fiscal year-end 2025-09-30 (Garrison and Monnig F-code withholds tied to RSU vesting on FY end — routine). Signal classified ROUTINE_10B5_1. The three TRUE open-market sales (Monnig 9/9/25 $581K, Cavaleri 12/5/25 $496K, Wood 12/23/25 $997K) were NOT within 14 days of any earmark/budget calendar event in the script's catalog. They WERE timed mid-quarter between earnings (Feb 5, 2026 Q1 print fell outside their 14-day windows).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Timing-wise, the open-market sales appear routine, not pre-disclosure. The insider_vs_calendar m-source does not see informational asymmetry. The damning signal is not the SALES (they are small) but the ABSENCE of PURCHASES (CLSK-01).

rfm_tuples.R: Implied by buyback narrative: share repurchases support per-share value.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-check actual share count delta and overhanging dilution (convertibles, options, PSUs).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Common outstanding: 284.3M (9/30/25) → 256.6M (3/31/26), -9.7% via buyback. Anti-dilutive overhang at 3/31/26: convertible notes 103,941,450 sh; Series A preferred conversion 5,250,000 sh; warrants 1,604,559 sh; options 1,992,759 sh; RSUs 26,547,749 sh; PSUs additional. Total overhang ~139M sh. Effective fully-diluted (if-converted) share count if stock recovers above convertible strikes: 256.6 + 139 = ~395M sh, 54% HIGHER than current basic outstanding. The buyback removed 30.6M common shares but added 103.9M shares of convertible-overhang. Net diluted-equivalent share count INCREASED.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Second Mode-B catch with severe implications. The 'buyback' is not a buyback in any meaningful sense — it is a stealth equity issuance, since the company sold call options worth >103M shares to buy back 30.6M shares. Anyone reading the headline 'CleanSpark deploys $1.15B convertible to repurchase stock' would think share count is going DOWN. The honest accounting is that fully-diluted share count went UP, by ~73M net. This is exactly the kind of complexity-disclosure gap the framework is built to catch.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-Q Note (Property and Equipment) and impairment expense lines: 'In March 2026, the Company concluded that a $4,008 deposit towards the purchase of transformers was no longer expected to be utilized and recorded an impairment charge for the full carrying amount. In December 2025, the Company began disposing of certain aged mining equipment for less than its carrying value and recorded a related impairment on idle equipment totaling $1,398.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B — verify implied capacity / business-condition signal. Aged-miner disposals and transformer-deposit impairments suggest infrastructure plans being scaled back.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total impairments H1 FY26: $5.4M ($4M transformers + $1.4M aged miners). Magnitude is small relative to balance sheet ($2.91B total assets) but directional. Combined with reduced power/land expansion language ('remainder intended for expansion of our power and land portfolio' in 10-K describes intent but Q3 10-Q shows minimal capex acceleration), suggests CLSK is throttling growth investment to fund the buyback.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honestly disclosed but the transformer impairment is unusual — it implies CLSK ordered transformers (long lead-time infrastructure), then in March 2026 decided it no longer needed them. Most miners are doing the opposite (accelerating power buildout). The contradiction between 'buyback proceeds will fund power/land expansion' (per 10-K) and 'transformer deposit impaired because no longer expected to be utilized' (per Q3 10-Q) is a Mode-B narrative gap. Either growth was throttled or the disclosure is imprecise about how proceeds were actually used.

supplemental_signals.mar_2026_series_a_amendment: Extinguished 2%-of-EBITA quarterly dividend for one-time $30K payment (related-party)

summary: CLSK is a -31% drawdown bitcoin miner where Mode-B forensic analysis identifies a SEVERE insider/narrative asymmetry. Despite a Nov-2025 $1.15B zero-coupon convertible whose proceeds were used to repurchase $463M of common stock (the textbook 'we believe our stock is undervalued' capital-allocation signal), ZERO insiders made an open-market purchase (code P) in the 12 months pre-cutoff — across 58 Form 4 filings and 162 transactions parsed. Insiders sold $2.07M (code S), got option-exercise/tax-withholding flow ($-7M of F/M activity), and the outgoing CEO Bradford received a 1.73M-share separation grant with continuing-compliance vesting clauses (atypical for a 'resignation'). The buyback itself is severely mischaracterized: it removed 30.6M common shares but added 103.9M shares of convertible-call-option overhang at $14.80/$19.16 strikes (already in the money for option-holders if stock recovers), so fully-diluted share count INCREASED ~73M net — a stealth equity issuance dressed as a buyback. Series A preferred (Schultz Irrevocable Trust, 45 votes/sh, ~31% voting power) had its 2%-of-EBITA dividend extinguished by Board in Mar 2026 for $30K — related-party amendment without independent-director-only disclosure. Honest positives: ICFR effective with 4 FY24 material weaknesses remediated, auditor upgraded MaloneBailey -> BDO USA, BTC FV loss honestly recognized, no going-concern flag. Severity counts: 2 PASS, 0 UNVERIFIABLE, 5 MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY, 2 SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY, 0 RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE. Verdict: SHORT-tier — this is the cleanest insider/narrative asymmetry in a SP600 distress name: management deploying $463M of investor capital on a buyback they refused to personally participate in.
